newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends higher vs dollar, ending run.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends higher vs dollar, ending run.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee ended 10 days of losses to close higher against the dollar because of selling pressure on the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.03 compared with its previous close of 57.15 and an opening of 57.12.
"There was great downward pressure on the dollar with more selling than buying," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Selling pressure mounted on the dollar after the Central Bank showed it was intent on holding the upside at 57.15 this week, she said.
The dollar exchange rate fluctuated between 57.00 and 57.13 rupees during the day, with most of trades around 57.03, dealers said.
The dollar is expected to ease further next week because of high local money rates, they said.
Overnight call money closed at 19 percent after opening at 16.5 percent, when about five big borrowers entered the market, dealers said.
